summary: Markets posted modest gains Wednesday after July CPI data met expectations, rising 3.4% year-over-year and cooling slightly from June's 3.5% pace. The in-line inflation print kept Federal Reserve officials divided on rate policy following July's contentious 9-3 vote to hold rates at 3.5%-3.75%, where three regional presidents dissented in favor of a hike. AI infrastructure stocks drove the session's strength, with CoreWeave surging 20% on stronger-than-expected sales and Super Micro Computer advancing 15% after topping revenue forecasts. Bitcoin held above $64,000 while ethereum traded near $1,915 as crypto investors scaled back September rate hike expectations following last week's disappointing jobs report. The benign inflation data gives Chair Warsh breathing room, though geopolitical tensions around U.S.-Iran negotiations and Middle East energy supply remain a persistent headwind across risk assets.

signals.title: July CPI rises 3.4% year-over-year, matching expectations
signals.desc: Headline inflation cooled slightly from June's 3.5% but core CPI rose 0.2% monthly, keeping Fed officials split on whether to resume rate hikes in September.

signals.title: Fed holds rates at 3.5%-3.75% with three hawkish dissents
signals.desc: Three FOMC members voted to hike in July amid persistent inflation concerns, marking rare dissent under Chair Warsh and weighing on duration-sensitive assets.

signals.title: AI infrastructure stocks surge on strong earnings beats
signals.desc: CoreWeave jumped 20% and Super Micro Computer rallied 15% after both companies posted better-than-expected revenue results, driving tech sector gains.

signals.title: Crypto holds gains as rate hike expectations fade post-CPI
signals.desc: Bitcoin maintained levels above $64,000 and ethereum near $1,915 as traders reduced bets on a September rate increase following weak July jobs data and tame inflation.

signals.title: U.S.-Iran impasse raises energy supply concerns
signals.desc: Stalled negotiations over Strait of Hormuz reopening and hardening demands around war compensation pressured equities Tuesday, with oil prices rising on supply risk.

verdict: Stocks grind higher on in-line CPI as AI earnings offset Fed uncertainty, but geopolitical risks and divided FOMC keep the rally tentative.
